newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ASC loses fight for delay on Hannes hearing.
newsitem.headline: ASC loses fight for delay on Hannes hearing.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) and prosecutors lost a fight on Monday to delay a committal hearing of insider trading charges against Macquarie Bank Ltd corporate advisory executive Simon Hannes.
The delay means the prosecution may be forced to present its case for Hannes'committal to trial without key documents from Macquarie Bank and TNT Ltd about the takeover bid for TNT.
Hannes is alleged to have used the information about Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV's (KPN) successful A$2.45 a share takeover bid to trade in TNT options, making a notional A$2 million profit.

St James local court Magistrate Deborah Sweeney ruled that the prosecution must present its full case to commit Hannes for trial on the insider trading charges on Tuesday morning, rejecting the prosecution's plea for a delay to Thursday.
The prosecution said it needed the delay to give 48 hours notice to Macquarie Bank and TNT Ltd before the previously confidential documents could be released to the court.
The prosecution told the court the ASC had an agreement with Macquarie and TNT not to release the papers before the companies' lawyers had been given a chance to object to their release if necessary.

Hannes' lawyer argued the prosecution had had plenty of time to get the documents released and that the charges were too serious and the level of "notoriety" now ascribed to Hannes over the alleged offences was too high for further delay.

Hannes, an executive in Macquarie's corporate advisory section, has been charged with insider trading after he allegedly bought A$2.00 TNT Ltd call options in the name of Mark Booth before the successful takeover bid.
He is also charged with trying to conceal transactions linked to the options trades.
Macquarie advised TNT on the takeover but Hannes was not involved with the TNT account as he was on extended leave at the time.
Hannes is alleged to have known about the impending KPN takeover bid for TNT at the time he bought the shares in the name of Mark Booth.
Documents in Booth's name but in Hannes' handwriting and on Hannes' laptop computer show Hannes was Booth, the ASC has alleged.
Hannes used his magnetic access key to enter Macquarie's Corporate Finance area at night six times in August and September last year, it is alleged.
The takeover was announced on October 2.

The ASC announced in January charges would be laid against Hannes, shocking Australia's financial markets which had watched Hannes rise through the ranks at Macquarie and orchestrate the mammoth and complex RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd merger in 1995.
Hannes is due to enter a plea on the financial transactions charges on Friday. Hannes' lawyers have indicated he would plead not guilty to the financial transactions charges.
Hannes faces up to five years in jail and/or a A$200,000 fine if convicted of insider trading.
